source_text: Necesse est igitur usque illis Apostolum ostendi, quem ego et in secunda Corinthiorum talem defendam, qualem in omnibus literis novi, qui et in prima, primus omnium templum Dei dedicavit: Non scitis vos templum Dei esse, et in vobis Dominum habitare? qui et templo sanciendo, purificandoque aeditualem legem scripsit: Si quis templum Dei vitiaverit, vitiabit illum Deus: templum enim Dei sanctum est quod estis vos. Age jam quis omnino vitiatum Deo redintegravit, id est traditum Satanae in interitum carnis, cum idcirco substruxerit: Nemo seducat semetipsum, id est, nemo praesumat vitiatum Deo redintegrari denuo posse; sicut rursus inter caetera, imo et ante caetera, moechos et fornicatores et molles et masculorum concubitores negans regnum consecuturos, praemisit: Ne erraveritis, scilicet si putaveritis eos consecuturos. Quibus autem regnum adimitur, utique nec vita permittitur, quae inest regno. Etiam ingerens: Sed in haec quidem fuistis; sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis in nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi, et in spiritu Dei nostri. Quanto delicta ista ante lavacrum accepto facit, tanto post lavacrum irremissibilia constituit; siquidem denuo ablui non licet. Agnosce et in sequentibus Paulum, columnam immobilem disciplinarum: Cibi ventri, et venter cibis; Deus et hunc et illos conficit; corpus autem non fornicationi, sed Deo. Faciamus enim hominem, ait Deus, ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram: et fecit hominem Deus ad imaginem et similitudinem Dei fecit illum. Dominus corpori; et sermo enim, caro factus est. Deus autem et Dominum suscitavit, et nos suscitabit per virtutem suam; propter corporis scilicet nexum cum illo. Et ideo: Non scitis corpora vestra membra Christi? quia et Christus Dei templum: Evertite templum hoc, et ego illud in triduo resuscitabo. Auferens membra Christi, faciam membra fornicariae? Non scitis quod qui adglutinatur fornicariae, unum corpus efficitur? Erunt enim duo in unam carnem. Qui autem adglutinatur Domino, unus est spiritus. Fugite fornicationem. Si revocabilem venia, quomodo fugiam, moechus denuo futurus? nihil profecero, si eam fugero; unum ero corpus, cui communicando adglutinabor. Omne delictum quod admiserit homo, extra corpus est; qui autem fornicatur, in corpus suum peccat. Ac ne hoc dictum in licentia fornicationis invaderes, ut in rem tuam, non Domini, delicturus, aufert te tibi, et Christo, sicut disposuerat, adjicit: Et non estis vestri; statim apponens: Empti enim estis pretio, sanguine scilicet Domini; glorificate et tollite Dominum in corpore vestro. Hoc qui praecipit, vide an ignoverit ei qui dedecoravit Dominum, et qui ejecerit eum de corpore suo, et quidem per incestum. Si vis omnem notitiam Apostoli ebibere, ut intelligas quanta securi censurae omnem sylvam libidinum caedat, et eradicet, et excaudicet, ne quidquam de recidivo fruticare permittat, adspice illum a justa fruge naturae, a matrimonii dico pomo, animas jejunare cupientem. De quibus autem scripsistis, bonum est homini mulierem non contingere: sed propter fornicationem unusquisque uxorem suam habeat; vir uxori, et uxor viro debitum reddat. Hujus boni fibulam quis illum nesciat invitum relaxasse, ut fornicationi obviam isset, quam si cui indulsit vel indulget, utique consilium remedii sui infregit, et tenebitur jam fraenandis continentiae conjugiis, si fornicatio, ob quam permittuntur, non timebitur; non enim timebitur quae ignoscetur. Et tamen ignovisse se profitetur matrimonii usum, non imperasse: vult enim omnes sibi adhaerere. Si autem licita ignoscuntur, illicita qui sperant? Innuptis quoque et viduis bonum esse dicit exemplo ejus perseverare; si vero deficerent, nubere, quia praeest nubere quam uri. Quibus oro ignibus deterius est uri? concupiscentiae, an poenae? Atquin, si fornicatio habet veniam, non urit concupiscentia ejus: Apostoli autem magis est poenae ignibus providere. Quod si poena est quae urit, ergo veniam non habet fornicatio, quam manet poena. Interea et divortium prohibens, pro eo aut viduitatis perseverantiam, aut reconciliationem pacis dominico praecepto adversus moechiam procurat, quia qui dimiserit uxorem praeter caussam moechiae, facit eam moechari; et qui dimissam a viro ducit, moechatur. Quanta remedia Spiritus Sanctus instaurat, ne id scilicet denuo admittatur, quod ignosci denuo non vult! Jam si usquequaque optimum dicit homini sic esse: Junctus es uxori, ne quaesieris solutionem, ut moechiae locum non des. Solutus es ab uxore, ne quaesieris uxorem, ut opportunitatem tibi serves. Quod et si duxeris uxorem, et si nupserit virgo, non peccat; pressuram tamen carnis habebunt hujusmodi. Et hic parcendo permittit. Caeterum, tempus in collecto constituit, ut et qui habent uxores, sic sint tanquam non habentes; praeterit enim habitus hujus mundi, jam scilicet non desiderantis: Crescite et multiplicamini. Sic vult nos praeter sollicitudinem degere, quia innupti de Domino curent, quomodo placeant Deo; nupti vero de mundo recogitent, quomodo placeant conjugio. Sic melius facere pronuntiat virginis conservatorem, quam erogatorem; sic et illam beatiorem decernit quae, amisso viro, fidem ingressa, amaverit occasionem viduitatis; sic haec omnia continentiae consilia ut divina commendat: Puto, inquit, et ego spiritum Dei habeo. Quis iste est assertor audacissimus omnis impudicitiae, moechorum et fornicatorum et incestorum plane fidelissimus advocatus, quibus honorandis suscepit hanc caussam adversus Spiritum Sanctum, ut falsum testimonium recitet de apostolo ejus? Nihil tale Paulus indulsit, qui totam carnis necessitatem de probis etiam titulis obliterare conatur. Indulget sane non adulteria, sed nuptias: parcit sane matrimoniis, non stupris: tentat ne naturae quidem ignoscere, ne culpae blandiatur; studet compescere benedictionis concubitum, ne maledictionis excusetur. Hoc ei supererat, carnem vel a sordibus purgare; a maculis enim non potest. Sed est hoc solemne perversis et idiotis et haereticis, jam et psychicis universis, alicujus capituli ancipitis occasione, adversus exercitum sententiarum instrumenti totius armari.
pass_a_gloss: It is necessary therefore to show the Apostle even to those, whom I will defend as such in the second to the Corinthians, as I know him to be in all his writings, who also in the first, being the first of all, dedicated the temple of God: Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Lord dwells in you? Who also, by sanctifying and purifying the temple, wrote the law for the priest: If anyone corrupts the temple of God, God will corrupt him: for the temple of God, which you are, is holy. Now who has restored to God what has been corrupted, that is, what has been handed over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, since he has built it up for this purpose: Let no one deceive himself, that is, let no one presume that what has been corrupted to God can be restored again; just as, among other things, indeed even before other things, he denies that the fornicators and adulterers and the effeminate and the males who lie with males will inherit the kingdom, having said beforehand: Lest you err, certainly if you think that they will inherit. To whom the kingdom is taken away, certainly life is not permitted, which is in the kingdom. Also adding: But you were such; but you were washed, but you were sanctified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in the Spirit of our God. How much more does he make these sins irremissible after baptism, as he did before baptism, since it is not permitted to be washed again. Recognize also in the following Paul, the immovable column of disciplines: Food is for the belly, and the belly is for food; God will destroy both this and that; but the body is not for fornication, but for God. For God said: Let us make man in our image and likeness; and God made man in the image and likeness of God. The Lord is for the body; and the word became flesh. But God raised the Lord, and will raise us through his power; on account of the bond of the body with him. And therefore: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Because Christ is also the temple of God: Destroy this temple, and I will raise it up in three days. Taking away the members of Christ, shall I make them members of a fornicator? Do you not know that he who is joined to a fornicator becomes one body? For the two will be one flesh. But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit. Flee from fornication. If forgiveness is revocable, how shall I flee, being about to become an adulterer again? I will not profit anything, if I flee from it; I will be one body, to which I will be joined. Every sin that a man commits is outside the body; but he who fornicates sins against his own body. And lest this statement be invaded by the license of fornication, so that you may sin against your own thing, not against the Lord's, it takes you away from yourself, and adds you to Christ, as he had arranged: And you are not your own; immediately adding: For you were bought with a price, namely the blood of the Lord; glorify and carry the Lord in your body. He who commands this, does he forgive him who has dishonored the Lord, and who has cast him out of his body, and indeed through incest? If you want to drink all the knowledge of the Apostle, so that you may understand how much he cuts down and eradicates the whole forest of lusts with the censure of security, and does not permit anything to sprout again from what is cut down, look at him, who desires souls to fast from the just fruit of nature, I say from the apple of marriage. Concerning which he wrote: It is good for a man not to touch a woman; but on account of fornication, let each man have his own wife, and let the husband render the debt to the wife, and the wife to the husband. Who does not know that he unwillingly relaxed the bond of this good, so that he might oppose fornication, which if he indulges to anyone, he certainly breaks the counsel of his own remedy, and will be held back by the marriages of continence, if fornication, on account of which they are permitted, is not feared; for what is forgiven is not feared. And yet he professes to have forgiven the use of marriage, not to have commanded it: for he wants all to adhere to him. But if what is lawful is forgiven, what hope is there for what is unlawful? He also says that it is good for the unmarried and the widows to persevere in example; but if they fail, to marry, because it is better to marry than to burn. With what fires is it worse to burn? With the fires of concupiscence, or of punishment? But if fornication has forgiveness, it does not burn with concupiscence; the Apostle, however, provides more for the fires of punishment. But if it is punishment that burns, then fornication does not have forgiveness, which remains in punishment. Meanwhile, also prohibiting divorce, instead of which he procures either the perseverance of widowhood or the reconciliation of peace, according to the Lord's precept against adultery, because he who dismisses his wife, except for the cause of adultery, makes her commit adultery; and he who marries a woman dismissed by her husband commits adultery. How many remedies does the Holy Spirit establish, so that what he does not want to be forgiven again may not be admitted again! Now if he says that it is best for a man to be thus: You are joined to a wife, do not seek a divorce, lest you give place to adultery. You are free from a wife, do not seek a wife, lest you give opportunity to yourself. What he also permits, if you marry a wife, and if a virgin marries, they do not sin; yet they will have the pressure of the flesh. And here he permits, sparing. Moreover, he establishes a time for gathering, so that even those who have wives may be as if they did not have them; for the fashion of this world is passing away, now certainly not desiring: Increase and multiply. Thus he wants us to live without solicitude, because the unmarried care about the Lord, how they may please God; but the married think about the world, how they may please their marriage. Thus he pronounces the preserver of virginity to be better than the one who gives it away; thus he also decrees that she who, having lost her husband, has entered into faith and loved the opportunity of widowhood, is more blessed; thus he commends all the counsels of continence as divine: I think, he says, that I also have the Spirit of God. Who is this most audacious assertor of all impudicity, the most faithful advocate of adulterers and fornicators and incestuous people, who has undertaken this cause against the Holy Spirit, so that he may recite false testimony about his Apostle? Paul did not indulge in such things, who tries to obliterate the whole necessity of the flesh, even from good titles. He certainly indulges in marriages, not in adulteries; he spares marriages, not stuprs; he tries not even to forgive nature, lest he flatter fault; he strives to restrain the concubinage of blessing, lest he excuse that of malediction. This was left to him, to purify the flesh even from filth; for he cannot from stains. But this is a solemn thing for the perverse and the ignorant and the heretics, now also for all the psychics, on the occasion of some ambiguous chapter, to arm themselves against the army of sentences of the whole instrument.

pass_b_english: I must prove what the Apostle is like even to those people — the kind I defend in Second Corinthians, the kind I recognize in all his letters. In his first letter he was the very first to dedicate God's temple: 'Don't you know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit lives in you?' (1 Cor 3:16-17). By sanctifying and purifying that temple he laid down the rule for its priest: 'If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy that person; for God's temple is sacred, and you are that temple.' So tell me — who has ever restored to God what was corrupted, that is, handed over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, since Paul built up this rule precisely so that 'no one should deceive himself' — meaning no one should presume that what has been corrupted before God can be restored again (1 Cor 3:17-18)?

Right alongside this, indeed before everything else, he bars fornicators, adulterers, the effeminate, and men who lie with males from inheriting the kingdom, prefacing it with: 'Do not be deceived — if you think they will inherit, you are wrong' (1 Cor 6:9-10). Those who lose the kingdom certainly lose the life that belongs to it. Then he adds: 'That is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God' (1 Cor 6:11). The more he made those sins serious before baptism, the more he makes them irremissible after baptism — since no one can be washed again.

Recognize Paul again in what follows: the immovable pillar of discipline. 'Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food, and God will destroy them both' — but the body is not for sexual immorality; it is for the Lord (1 Cor 6:13). 'Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness' (Gen 1:26) — and God created mankind in his own image. The Lord is for the body, and the Word became flesh (John 1:14). God raised the Lord and will raise us by his power, because of the body's union with him. That is why: 'Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ?' (1 Cor 6:15). Since Christ is God's temple too: 'Destroy this temple, and I will raise it in three days' (John 2:19). Shall I take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? Don't you know that he who unites himself with a prostitute becomes one body with her? For 'the two will become one flesh' (Gen 2:24). But whoever is united with the Lord becomes one spirit with him (1 Cor 6:16-17). 'Flee from sexual immorality' (1 Cor 6:18). If forgiveness is revocable, how can I flee — since I would just become an adulterer again? I gain nothing by fleeing; I would still be one body with her. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body (1 Cor 6:18).

Lest this statement be hijacked as a license for immorality — so that you sin against what is yours, not the Lord's — Paul takes you away from yourself and adds you to Christ, as he arranged: 'You are not your own; you were bought at a price, the blood of the Lord. Therefore honor God with your body' (1 Cor 6:19-20). Does the one who commands this forgive the man who has dishonored the Lord and cast him out of his body — and that through incest?

If you want to swallow all the Apostle's teaching, so you can see how thoroughly he cuts down and eradicates the whole forest of lusts with the axe of censure, allowing nothing to sprout from the stumps — look at him urging souls to fast from the legitimate fruit of nature, I mean the apple of marriage. 'It is good for a man not to have sexual relations with a woman' (1 Cor 7:1). Yet 'because of sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife and each woman her own husband. The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband' (1 Cor 7:2-3). Who doesn't know that he reluctantly loosened the bond of this good precisely to oppose fornication? But if he indulges it for anyone, he breaks the counsel of his own remedy and will be held back by marriages of continence — if fornication, the very reason they are permitted, is not feared; for what is forgiven is not feared. And yet he claims to have conceded the use of marriage, not commanded it — because he wants all to cling to him. But if what is lawful is conceded, what hope is there for what is unlawful?

He also says it is good for the unmarried and widows to remain as he does; but if they cannot exercise self-control, they should marry, 'for it is better to marry than to burn' (1 Cor 7:8-9). Burn with what fire — lust or punishment? But if fornication has forgiveness, it does not burn with lust; yet the Apostle provides for the fires of punishment. If it is punishment that burns, then fornication has no forgiveness — it remains under punishment. Meanwhile, by forbidding divorce he secures either the perseverance of widowhood or reconciliation, by the Lord's command against adultery: 'Anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, makes her the victim of adultery, and anyone who marries a divorced woman commits adultery' (Matt 19:9). How many remedies the Holy Spirit establishes, so that what he refuses to forgive again may never be admitted again!

Now if he says the best thing for a man is to stay as he is: 'Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be free. Are you free from a wife? Do not seek a wife' (1 Cor 7:27) — lest you give occasion to adultery or opportunity to yourself. Yet he permits: if you marry, and if a virgin marries, they do not sin — though such people will have trouble in the flesh. Here he permits, sparingly. Further, he sets a fixed time: 'Those who have wives should live as if they had none' (1 Cor 7:29) — for the present form of this world is passing away, and certainly not desiring 'be fruitful and multiply' (Gen 1:28). He wants us to live without anxiety, because the unmarried care about the Lord's affairs — how to please the Lord — while the married care about worldly affairs — how to please their spouse (1 Cor 7:32-34). So he declares the guardian of virginity better than the one who gives it away; he judges the woman who, having lost her husband, embraced faith and loved the opportunity of widowhood, more blessed. Thus he commends all these counsels of continence as divine: 'I think that I too have the Spirit of God' (1 Cor 7:40).

Who is this most brazen champion of all impurity, the most faithful advocate of adulterers, fornicators, and incestuous people — who has taken up their cause against the Holy Spirit, so as to bear false witness about his Apostle? Paul conceded nothing of the sort — he who tries to obliterate the whole necessity of the flesh even from legitimate grounds. He concedes marriage, not adultery; he spares marriage, not debauchery. He tries not even to concede nature, lest he flatter fault; he strives to restrain the blessed conjugal act lest he excuse the cursed one. The most he could do was purify the flesh from filth — from stains he cannot. But this is a solemn farce for the perverse, the ignorant, the heretics, and now all the 'psychics' — seizing on some ambiguous chapter to arm themselves against the entire army of sentences of the whole instrument.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text, including the complex theological arguments regarding the irremissibility of sin after baptism and the distinction between marriage and fornication. All scripture citations in Pass B correctly identify the source material (e.g., 1 Cor 3:16-17, 1 Cor 6:9-10, Gen 1:26, John 1:14, Gen 2:24, 1 Cor 7:1-3, Matt 19:9, 1 Cor 7:27-40) and match the quoted or alluded content. The translator correctly handled the distinction between 'corpus' (body) and 'caro' (flesh) and preserved the author's polemical tone.
source: 'Non scitis vos templum Dei esse, et in vobis Dominum habitare?', English: 'Do you not know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit lives in you?'
